subject: Hosted embeddings: sudden p99 tail increase following catalog promotion — Greenfield escalation
messages:
From: Sara Taylor <sara.taylor@greenfield.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenfield SRE <sre@greenfield.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: embeddings latency spike (p95/p99) — noticed after your 01:05 UTC catalog push

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing a critical increase in p95 and p99 latency from the hosted embeddings endpoint starting at ~01:07 UTC this morning, right after you pushed the model-catalog promotion. The regression is primarily affecting our semantic search pipeline — overall throughput is fine but tail latency spikes to 1.2s from a steady 160ms baseline, and we saw around 0.8% timeouts in our batch consumers which is breaking some downstream requests.

Attached is a small sample of request_ids and a CSV of traces (greenfield_traces_0620.csv). We've also included a couple of example request chains where the embedding call is the blocker. This is impacting our search relevance experiments and causing a backlog.

Can you confirm whether anything in the catalog promotion could have affected runtime behavior (quantization flags, KV cache layout, or new kernel selection)? We need an ETA for mitigation or a roll-back — this is customer-impacting and we're escalating internally.

Thanks — would appreciate an update in the next 30 minutes

Sara Taylor
Head of ML Engineering, Greenfield AI
[sent from iPhone]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Taylor <sara.taylor@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: embeddings latency spike (p95/p99) — noticed after your 01:05 UTC catalog push

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and for the traces. I'm escalating this to our engineering and SRE leads (cc'd) to triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Internal Triage: Marissa and Marcus to run correlation against the 01:05 UTC catalog promotion and check model variant metadata, kernel selection, and KV cache warming.
- Quick Mitigation: If a model variant promotion correlates, we'll prepare a rollback to the previous catalog snapshot and test on a canary before full rollback.
- Customer remediation: we'll prioritize a canary rollback and share an ETA within 30 minutes. If you want an active bridge, we can do a 20-minute call at 10:00 AM PT.

I forwarded the CSV to engineering (attachment: engineer_trace_bundle_0620.zip) — Marissa/Marcus, please confirm whether the trace IDs show increased decode time or cache misses.

Jordan Blake

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: embeddings latency spike (p95/p99) — initial triage notes

Jordan / Marcus — quick notes from the first pass after running the provided traces against infra logs:  

- Correlation: the spike aligns exactly with the catalog promotion at 2028-06-20T01:05:12Z (UTC). The promoted model variant changed quantization metadata and the runtime kernel selector opted into a different attention kernel for that architecture.
- Root signal: the slow path appears to be increased KV cache misses combined with a small, but systematic, decode CPU increase for long sequences. The combination amplifies tail latency under bursty arrival patterns used by Greenfield's batched pipeline.
- Evidence: sample trace request_ids show per-request embed compute rising from ~120ms -> ~850-1200ms at p99; no significant increase in GPU queueing or network egress.

Actionables recommended:  
1) Canary rollback: revert that specific catalog entry to the previous model variant (we have snapshot catalog_20280620_0102). Test canary at 50 qps for 10 minutes.
2) If rollback is delayed, we can apply a temporary routing policy to route Greenfield traffic to a compatible variant in a different pool (adds ~20ms but reduces tails).
3) Short-term config: lower batch sizes for Greenfield's route to reduce batching variance.

I've started the rollback job in dry-run; Marcus, can you validate the canary after I flip it? Link to runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-runbook-embed-kvcache (internal). I've zipped the extended traces and annotated logs: engineer_trace_bundle_0620.zip

Subject: Re: embeddings latency spike (p95/p99) — remediation plan and next steps

Sara — quick update and plan of record:  

Summary:
- Triage (engineering): We confirmed the p99 tail regressions correlate with the catalog promotion at 01:05 UTC and a model-variant metadata change that influenced kernel selection and cache warming behavior. The spike is not caused by GPU saturation.

Immediate remediation (in progress):
1) Canary rollback to catalog snapshot catalog_20280620_0102 — canary running now at 50 qps.
2) If canary looks good (10 minutes), we'll roll the route back to the previous variant for Greenfield and monitor p95/p99 for 30 minutes.
3) As a contingency, we can apply a per-route batch-size override to reduce variance.

Customer impact & compensation:
- We recognize this is customer-impacting. We're offering an immediate transient quota bump to help clear Greenfield's backlog (no extra charge for today).
- After stabilization we'll open a postmortem and share technical details and compensatory credit recommendations for your account team.

Call options: we can jump on a 15-minute bridge at 11:30 AM PT to walk through the change and timeline — please confirm if you want the call.

I'll follow up with monitoring screenshots and the JIRA ticket for tracking (RED-8921).

Thanks for flagging this quickly; apologies for the disruption — we'll keep this prioritized.

Jordan Blake
